budget.always: Always, at every level: acceptance criteria, tests, quality gates, source verification, and security checks remain mandatory; if a saving would harm quality, do not apply it and say so.
budget.rule.light.0: Read only relevant files and sections; search before reading (catalog with search.mjs, code with targeted search).
budget.rule.light.1: Reuse results already verified in this session instead of repeating reads or searches.
budget.rule.light.2: Concise reports: outcome, evidence, open issues; no context repetitions.
budget.rule.max.0: No agents: everything in the main session, unless the user requests them.
budget.rule.max.1: "Fast" profile for mechanical or formatting tasks; otherwise "standard" (deep-review only if risk is high).
budget.rule.max.2: Propose deterministic scripts for every repeatable check instead of doing it manually.
budget.rule.medium.0: At most one agent, and only for a truly independent part; handoffs with structured-handoff (references, not copies).
budget.rule.medium.1: "Standard" profile for ordinary work; "deep-review" only for architecture, tricky debugging, or high risk.
budget.rule.medium.2: A single review round: after the quality gate, re-check only what changed.

install.usage:
Usage:
  install.mjs <github-link | owner/repo | folder> [options]     install skills/agents
  install.mjs --update [name ...]                               update from the same links
  install.mjs --remove <name ...> [--kind skill|agent] --yes    remove installed items
  install.mjs --list                                            list installed items
  install.mjs --approve <name ...> [--kind skill|agent]         analyze and approve installed version

Installation options:
  --only a,b                  install only these names
  --all                       install everything found in link
  --to global|agent:<name>[,agent:<name>]
                              where to assign skills (default: prompts; outside terminal: global)
  --category a,b              categories (default: deduced from description)
  --ref <branch|tag|sha>      version to install
  --path <subfolder>          limit search to a subfolder of repo
  --package                   install full package (the repo or --path subfolder, with all
                              shared files) instead of just skill folders; contains all its skills
  --kind skill|agent          limit to one kind
  --dry-run [--json]          show what would be found and risk, without writing anything
  --scan                      with --dry-run: also analyze with NVIDIA SkillSpector (with --only, only those)
  --force                     overwrite an existing external item / locally modified
  --expect-commit <sha>       abort if repo is no longer at that commit (used by UI to install
                              exactly what the preview showed)
  --sync                      run sync.mjs on completion

Security: before installing or updating, each item is checked by NVIDIA SkillSpector according to
settings.json (security.skillspector: block | warn | off). With "block", items judged DO_NOT_INSTALL
by SkillSpector are not installed, nor if analysis fails or SkillSpector is missing.

settings.dependencies.claudeMayInstall.h: If a skill or agent requires a missing program (e.g. ffmpeg), Claude installs it automatically with "npm run needs -- --install". Only programs listed in dependencies.json, using the command built by the hub (winget, brew, npm or uv): never commands written by a skill. Disabled: Claude asks you before installing. Claude Code may still ask you to approve the command.

settings.quality.improvements.help: Propose: Claude presents suggestions to you and you decide. Apply to my skills: Claude automatically modifies your own skills, agents, and workflows (skills/own, agents/own, workflows), then runs doctor and tests and shows you what changed. Third-party items are never modified, and nothing is pushed to GitHub without your confirmation.
settings.quality.improvements.label: What to do with identified improvements
settings.quality.recordEvaluations.help: After self-critique, Claude records in evaluations/<computer>.jsonl scores per point, the quality gate outcome, retry attempts, and whether the chosen workflow was right. "npm run evaluate -- report" shows recurring weak points, regressions, skills to review, and duplicates; before a similar task Claude receives a heads-up. Only summarized requests and numbers, never secrets. Disabled: does not record or warn.
settings.quality.recordEvaluations.label: Record evaluations for each task and use them to improve
settings.quality.selfCritique.help: After the quality gate, Claude critically reviews the outcome and how it was achieved: weaknesses, unverified assumptions, better alternatives, weak points of skills, agents, and workflows used, with up to 3 concrete proposals. "At each phase" is more accurate but uses more tokens. Skipped for small tasks.

settings.security.skillspector.help: Block: every skill or agent from GitHub is scanned; if SkillSpector says "do not install", if the scan fails, or if SkillSpector is missing, it is not installed. Warn: scans if SkillSpector is present and shows the result, but does not block. Off: no scan (hub checks still apply).

settings.security.skillspectorLlm.help: In addition to static analysis, SkillSpector has an AI model inspect the skill (more accurate, slower). Requires SKILLSPECTOR_PROVIDER configured in the environment (e.g. claude_cli, anthropic): see the SkillSpector guide.

settings.tokens.savingLevel.help: Off (default): the system operates normally, quality first. Light: targeted reads and brief reports. Medium: additionally at most one agent and the most capable model only for difficult tasks. Maximum: additionally no agents and the fast model for mechanical tasks. At every level, criteria, tests, quality gate, source verification, and security checks remain mandatory. Claude reads this via "npm run route" (scripts/lib/budget.mjs).
settings.tokens.savingLevel.label: Token saving level
settings.usage.fromTranscripts.help: Reads sessions saved by Claude Code on this machine solely to count how many times each hub skill or agent is used. ui.welcome.intro: A few choices and your hub is ready. You can change everything later in Settings.
ui.welcome.mayInstall: Your AI assistant may install missing programs
ui.welcome.mayInstallHint: only programs declared in dependencies.json, with commands built by the hub
ui.welcome.noTools: No AI tool chosen: nothing installed. Pick at least one tool above.
ui.welcome.programs: Programs (Git, Node, FFmpeg, SkillSpector…) are installed only from a terminal with "npm run setup", which shows every command before running it.
ui.welcome.security.block: Block: install nothing that is not scanned and approved (recommended)
ui.welcome.security.off: Off: no scan (the hub's own checks still run)
ui.welcome.security.warn: Warn: scan when possible, never block
ui.welcome.securityHint: Skills and agents downloaded from GitHub can be scanned with NVIDIA SkillSpector (optional program, Apache-2.0, installed with npm run setup).
ui.welcome.syncFailed: The installation into your AI tools failed: see the details below.
ui.welcome.title: Welcome to AI Hub
ui.welcome.toolsHint: The hub installs its skills and agents into each tool you pick. Codex and OpenCode share the open Agent Skills folder (~/.agents/skills); Antigravity CLI reads ~/.gemini/config/skills.
update.confirmRequiredNoTty: A confirmation and a terminal are required: add --yes to send without asking.
update.missingProgramsNotice:
This computer is missing programs used by skills: {programs}.
    Install them once with: npm run setup (installs only what is missing, asking for confirmation)
update.needsSetupNotice: Dependencies have changed: run "npm run setup" to install what is missing.
update.pullHint: To download them: npm run update -- --pull
update.pushHint: To send them: npm run update -- --push
update.syncHint: To apply updates to Claude Code: npm run sync
usage.adviceAgentContext: Runs in a separate context: instructions (approx. {body} tokens) are combined with files read and the report. Use it for independent, substantial parts (broad research, standalone reviews), not for tiny changes.
usage.adviceExtraFiles: Contains other files (approx. {extra} tokens): only read when needed; ask to read only relevant parts.
usage.adviceHeavy: Heavy: approx. {body} tokens each time it is used. Use it for medium or large tasks; for small tasks it is better to avoid it.
usage.adviceLongDescriptionOwn: Long description (approx. {desc} tokens in every session): shorten it, keeping what it does and when to use it.
usage.adviceLongDescriptionThird: Long description (approx. {desc} tokens in every session): from a third party; consider if you really need it.
usage.adviceMostUsed: Among the most used: worth maintaining carefully (tests, self-critique) as it impacts many tasks.
usage.adviceNotUsed90: No usage in the last 90 days: description of {what} takes approx. {desc} tokens in every session. If unneeded, disconnect or remove it.
usage.adviceOftenUsedNotApproved: Frequently used but unapproved: inspect with SkillSpector and approve it (Install tab).
usage.machineCounts: Counts for this computer: usage/{machine}.json{updated} · transcripts read: {files}
usage.noUsageRecorded: ℹ No usage recorded so far: usage tips will appear once data is available.
usage.perSessionTokens: Descriptions of all skills and agents: approx. {perSession} tokens in each Claude Code session.
usage.trackingOff: ℹ Transcript counting turned off (Settings → Usage and consumption): showing previously saved counts.
